definitions.explanation: A building or hall where religious ceremonies, rituals, or festivals are conducted. Used for both Shinto and Buddhist contexts, as well as more broadly for any sacred or ceremonial space.

examples.japanese: {祭殿|さいでん}で{神事|しんじ}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A Shinto ritual was performed in the ceremonial hall.

examples.japanese: {祭殿|さいでん}の{前|まえ}に{参拝者|さんぱいしゃ}が{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Worshippers are lined up in front of the ceremonial hall.

examples.japanese: {古代|こだい}の{祭殿|さいでん}の{跡|あと}が{発掘|はっくつ}{調査|ちょうさ}で{発見|はっけん}され、{当時|とうじ}の{祭祀|さいし}の{様子|ようす}を{知|し}る{手|て}がかりとなった。
examples.english: The remains of an ancient ceremonial hall were discovered in an excavation, providing clues about the rituals of the time.

notes:
A compound of {祭|さい} (festival/ritual) and {殿|でん} (hall/palace). Refers to a building or space specifically designated for conducting religious ceremonies or rituals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祭殿|さいでん}で{祀|まつ}る: enshrine in a ceremonial hall
- {祭殿|さいでん}を{建|た}てる: build a ceremonial hall
- {祭殿|さいでん}の{中|なか}: inside the ceremonial hall

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {拝殿|はいでん}: worship hall (the hall in front of a shrine where visitors pray)
- {本殿|ほんでん}: main hall (the innermost building of a shrine housing the deity)
- {神殿|しんでん}: divine hall; temple (hall where a deity is enshrined)
- {社殿|しゃでん}: shrine buildings (collective term for the buildings of a Shinto shrine)
